_comment: Curated, roadmap-grounded feature suggestions for PhotoSphere AI. Tier 'high-impact' = the top next-best moves; tier 'backlog' = production/enterprise items further out. Clicking a card in the dashboard POSTs it to /api/queue, which appends a structured block to dashboard/FEATURE_QUEUE.md for the Planner/Developer agents to pick up in the next /orchestrate cycle.

suggestions.title: Ship the Reclassification UI (unblock Week 5–6)
suggestions.rationale: This is the single item currently blocking Week 5–6 from closing. Every backend endpoint it needs (folder lists with counts, folder photos with pre-signed thumbnails, move, create-folder, reclassify+poll) is already built and live-verified. It only needs a wireframe pick (Option A/B/C already drafted) and the page built against shipped endpoints.
suggestions.queues: Have Master surface the wireframe pick, then Developer builds design/wireframes/reclassify-ui.svg into a working page against the already-shipped collections/folders/reclassify endpoints. Short Tester pass on just that page.

suggestions.title: Core UI: Collection Dashboard + Storage Usage
suggestions.rationale: Week 7–8's headline item and the natural next surface after reclassification. Turns the tested backend into something a photographer can actually see: collection overview, per-folder counts, and real storage usage. Follows the UI-decision protocol (2–3 SVG approaches first).
suggestions.queues: Planner scopes a Core UI dashboard spec (collection overview cards, storage-usage meter, recent-activity strip). Developer posts 2–3 SVG wireframe approaches to STATUS.md and waits for a pick before building.

suggestions.title: Folder Browser + Fullscreen Photo Viewer (EXIF panel)
suggestions.rationale: The grid-view folder browser and fullscreen viewer are what make the product usable end-to-end. EXIF is already exposed on GET /api/photos/:id and pre-signed URLs (60s TTL) are enforced, so the data layer is ready — this is primarily a front-end build.
suggestions.queues: Planner scopes folder-browser grid + fullscreen viewer with EXIF info panel. Developer wireframes 2–3 approaches, gets a pick, builds against pre-signed-URL delivery. Include duplicate-detection warning surface for the pHash/sha256 verdicts already produced.

suggestions.title: Guest Access + OTP Approval System
suggestions.rationale: This is the core product differentiator — the whole 'share a folder with a client, owner approves via OTP' loop the MVP's Definition of Done is built around. Enterprise-grade from day one: capture device/IP/location on link click, owner approval dashboard, scoped guest sessions, one-tap revocation, folder-permission enforcement on every endpoint.
dependencies: Core UI (owner needs an approval dashboard)
suggestions.queues: Planner scopes the guest-invite → short-link → access-request → OTP-to-owner → approval → scoped-guest-session flow as a multi-pass spec, honoring the roadmap's security model (permission-check-then-pre-signed-URL, 60s TTL, audit trail). Flag the email-delivery dependency as a pending decision.

suggestions.title: Audit Log + Owner Activity Dashboard
suggestions.rationale: Records every view, download, and approval — the trust backbone for the sharing product and a hard prerequisite for any future enterprise/SOC 2 conversation. Owner sees who accessed what and when. Best built alongside or right after guest access so events exist to log.
suggestions.queues: Planner scopes an append-only audit-log table + owner activity dashboard (who/what/when, filterable). Developer builds event hooks on every photo/folder access and download path. Tester verifies no access path bypasses the log.

suggestions.title: GitHub Actions CI (lint + test on every PR)
suggestions.rationale: The GitHub remote is now connected but nothing enforces quality on PRs. A CI pipeline running tsc --noEmit, ESLint, and the smoke/regression suites on every PR turns the four-agent discipline into an automated gate — low effort, high leverage, and a prerequisite for ever pushing with confidence.
dependencies: explicit go-ahead to push to remote
suggestions.queues: Planner scopes a CI workflow spec (.github/workflows/ci.yml: install → lint → typecheck → test on PR, Postgres/Redis service containers). Developer authors it on a branch; do NOT push without Abhishek's explicit go-ahead per ground rules.

suggestions.title: Security Headers (Helmet) + Rate-Limit & Dependency Hardening
suggestions.rationale: Consolidates the launch-prep security items: Helmet.js security headers across all APIs, a final rate-limit audit on every endpoint (auth buckets are already split), and clearing the deferred Next.js 14.2.13 security advisory in a dedicated dependency-upgrade pass.
suggestions.queues: Planner scopes a security-hardening pass: Helmet headers, rate-limit coverage audit across all routes, and the Next.js advisory upgrade. Developer applies + adds regression tests; Tester verifies headers and limits live.

suggestions.title: Natural Language Search (CLIP semantic search)
suggestions.rationale: 'beach with sunset' style semantic search via CLIP embeddings — a marquee Phase 2 differentiator. Fits cleanly behind the existing swappable classification interface so it stays a local-first, one-module addition until real inference is approved.
suggestions.queues: Planner scopes a semantic-search spec: CLIP embedding generation in the BullMQ worker (mocked provider first, per the swappable-interface rule), vector storage, and a query endpoint. Keep everything local/offline until real model inference is signed off.

suggestions.title: Face Recognition — group photos by person
suggestions.rationale: Auto-group by person (DeepFace/face-api.js) — high-value organization feature and a strong retention hook for photographers. Runs async in the existing worker pipeline, same architecture as classification.
suggestions.queues: Planner scopes a face-grouping spec behind the swappable AI interface (mock first), with a pending decision on biometric-data privacy/consent handling. Async via BullMQ, never inline — same rules as classification.

suggestions.title: Bulk Operations (multi-select move / delete / download)
suggestions.rationale: Photographers work in hundreds of photos; single-photo actions don't scale. Multi-select move/delete/download is the most-requested quality-of-life feature once the folder browser exists, and it reuses the already-shipped move + folder endpoints.
suggestions.queues: Planner scopes bulk-select UX + batch endpoints (batch move/delete/download with a job for large sets). Developer wireframes selection patterns, gets a pick, builds with race-safe folder photoCount reconciliation (pattern already exists).

suggestions.title: Branded Client Portals (photographer-branded delivery)
suggestions.rationale: Lets photographers deliver via a branded page (custom logo/color) instead of the raw app — a direct monetization and differentiation lever that builds on the guest-access foundation.
suggestions.queues: Planner scopes a branded-portal spec (per-collection logo/color, client-facing delivery view layered on the guest-access session model). Developer wireframes the branded delivery surface, gets a pick, builds.

suggestions.title: SSO / SAML (Okta, Azure AD) — enterprise identity
suggestions.rationale: The gate for landing enterprise accounts. Adds SAML/OIDC login (Okta, Azure AD) alongside the existing opaque-token session model without disrupting it. Pairs naturally with the audit log for enterprise security reviews.
suggestions.queues: Planner scopes an SSO/SAML spec that layers enterprise IdP login over the current session model (opaque tokens preserved). Flag IdP-provider choice and JIT-provisioning rules as pending decisions.

suggestions.title: Team Workspaces — multiple owners, shared collections
suggestions.rationale: Moves the product from single-photographer to studio/agency accounts: multiple owners, shared collections, role-based permissions. The foundational schema change that most other Phase 3 enterprise features (SSO, white-label, analytics) build on.
suggestions.queues: Planner scopes an org/membership/role model spec (owner/member/viewer roles, shared-collection permissions) with a careful migration plan off the current single-owner schema. Flag the role matrix as a pending decision.

suggestions.title: Public REST API + Webhooks (B2B integrations)
suggestions.rationale: Turns PhotoSphere into a platform: programmatic access for B2B integrations plus webhooks that fire on classification events. Enables the Phase 4 marketplace play and creates an expansion-revenue surface.
suggestions.queues: Planner scopes a versioned public REST API (API-key auth distinct from session tokens) + a webhook delivery system (signed payloads, retries) triggered on classification/share events. Flag rate-limit and versioning policy as pending decisions.
